text:
marta: Quick async ask — can someone run a short microbench + quality sweep for redwood-v2 (prod candidate) under three quant profiles: int8, int4, fp8? Need p95 latency (8k seq) + sample_loss on longchat-200 set. Please run on rtx-pool and drop artifacts. cc @dave @junaid

dave: I can run this. confirm eval set = longchat-200 and batch sizes?

marta: yes longchat-200. run batch=1 and batch=8. Include no KV-priming run too if cheap. Also capture kernel logs and GPU util.

junaid: taking batch=1 first. will queue on rtx-pool:g3. Do you want warmup=20 steps?

marta: warmup=20 ok. use token cap 8192. keep sampling rng fixed (seed=42) so sample_loss is comparable.

sylvie: heads-up — I just merged a small scheduler tweak that might change int4 perf (PR #3245, commit abcdef1). If you want baseline, use commit before merge: git rev-parse HEAD~1 = 9f8e7d6.

dave: noted. I'll run both commits (pre-PR and post-PR) to isolate.

bench-bot: queued jobs -> 4589 (int8/post-PR), 4590 (int4/post-PR), 4591 (fp8/post-PR), 4592..4594 (same pre-PR). ETA ~35m. artifacts will be at https://bench.redwood/jobs/4589

bench-bot: results in — summary (post-PR, batch=1, 8k seq): int8 p95=78ms, int4 p95=52ms, fp8 p95=45ms. sample_loss deltas vs fp32 baseline (lower is better): int8 +0.02, int4 +0.12, fp8 +0.04. full artifacts: https://bench.redwood/jobs/4589/artifacts.zip

junaid: int4 sample_loss +0.12 is larger than I expected. can we get the top 5 prompts where int4 diverged?

dave: pulling top diffs now. attaching small excerpt:

```
PROMPT: "Summarize the author's stance on economic policy in the passage..."
FP32: "The author argues for targeted stimulus to bridge demand shortfalls..."
INT4: "The author wants to increase spending across the board..."  <-- hallucination shift
PROMPT: "Draft a polite email declining a partnership offer..."
FP32: "Thanks for reaching out. We're focusing on..."
INT4: "No thanks. We don't want that."  <-- tone & safety regression
```

syIvie: (typo) sylvie: I looked at kernel traces — int4 shows more hmux small-kernel paths; likely quantized matmul tiling mismatch. Suggest: try different input packing (pack=32->64) and a small bias-fix patch I can push.

marta: good catch. let's not ship int4 to canary until we either fix or add fallback. proposal: canary with fp8 only for 24-48h at 5-10% then widen. dave can you create canary route and a traffic policy that falls back to fp8 when sample_loss > 0.08?

dave: yes. creating canary: /model/redwood-v2/canary -> id abc123. Traffic split 10%. Fallback rule: if rolling sample_loss over 1k requests > 0.08 switch to fp8 variant. Ops will handle automation.

ops-bot: Canary created: id=abc123, route=/model/redwood-v2/canary, traffic=10%, monitor=sample_loss, alert-channel=#eng-runtime.

junaid: I'll run targeted diff runs with pack=64 + sylvie's bias-fix on pre-PR commit to see impact. ETA ~2h.

sylvie: pushed bias-fix branch: perf/bias-fix-int4 (branch hash b3f4a2). quick patch:
```
diff --git a/runtime/quant.c b/runtime/quant.c
index 7a1..e9b 100644
--- a/runtime/quant.c
+++ b/runtime/quant.c
@@ -212,6 +212,9 @@
     // adjust small-bias to reduce tail drift
-    bias = bias * 0.98;
+    // apply conservative bias correction for int4
+    bias = fmaf(bias, 0.985f, 0.0001f);
+    // end patch
```

dave: thanks. once junaid has numbers, we'll decide canary variant. marta: do you want a short PR note for the rollout?

marta: yes — include perf summary, top failure examples, and fallback policy. I'll post update to #eng-runtime and #product. :thumbsup:

bench-bot: update: junaid's pack=64 + bias-fix (pre-PR) run -> int4 sample_loss delta now +0.03, p95=55ms. artifacts: https://bench.redwood/jobs/4620

marta: excellent — that delta is acceptable. plan: ship scheduler tweak (post-PR), apply bias-fix, enable pack=64 for int4 in config, but still default canary to fp8 for initial 24h. Reopen thread if we see regressions. Thanks all.

dave: I'll open the canary rollout ticket and link PRs.

ops-bot: ticket created: CANARY-987, owner=dave, due=1971326400 (48h), watchers=[marta,sylvie,junaid].

marta: :raised_hands:
